newsitem.title: USA: FedEx sees little impact from FAA ruling.
newsitem.headline: FedEx sees little impact from FAA ruling.

text.p: Federal Express Corp said Tuesday it expects no material financial impact from a U.S. Federal Aviation Administration directive limiting payloads of Boeing Co 727 aircraft that have been converted from passenger to all-cargo operations.
However, the transportation company said it will seek approval for smaller containers not addressed by the FAA.

On Monday, the FAA proposed that operators reduce payloads per container from 8,000 pounds to 3,000 pounds after a final rule is issued until the 727's floor structure is modified or re-qualified to carry greater weight.
The FAA said it expects to issue a final rule by October.

"We've been discussing this matter with the FAA since late last year, and we've expected the proposed rule," Senior Vice President of Air Operations Gilbert Mook said in a statement. "We're confident we can operate our aircraft within current load limits either by modifications or by further demonstrating the safety of the aircraft to the FAA."
More than 90 percent of the cargo containers FedEx currently uses on these aircraft weigh less than the limits the FAA has proposed, the company said.

The vast majority of the company's containers currently meet the weight requirements of the FAA limits, though FedEx will seek approval for smaller "demi" containers which the FAA has not addressed in the proposal, it said.

"The high-value goods we carry tend to weigh much less than traditional freight carried by other cargo carriers; therefore we expect to be able to manage any impact of the proposed weight limits," Mook said. "In the meantime, we'll continue our discussions with the FAA."
